notes.title: Thank you, and a small request!
notes.notes:
Hi friends.  I've received so many nice comments about this game over the years, and I just wanted to say thank you.  It's so personally rewarding for me to hear stories of friends and families bonding together and having fun, and I'm so honored and thankful that I could be a small part of that.  I grew up in the pre-internet era playing Goldeneye and Mario Kart and old DOS games shoulder to shoulder with my friends, and I know how local-multiplayer just somehow feels better.

If you haven't already, would you please consider taking a minute and writing a brief review of the game?  I'm very close to the 500 review mark which is a considerable milestone in terms of Steam visibility.  

I would never ask you to lie or give a fake review.  But if the game has brought you some joy and you'd recommend it to others, taking just a minute or two to write what you liked and didn't like would really help me out.

notes.title: Hidden in Plain Sight Online -- public beta now available
notes.notes:
I have opened the beta testing for the new version of Hidden in Plain Sight to the public for the Windows version of the game.

If you opt into the beta, you will be able to [b]play online with up to 8 players total[/b].  There is a limitation to four Xbox-type controllers per machine, however.  I have [b]also added keyboard support[/b].

This is absolutely a BETA. There will be bugs! There will be sync issues! There will be crashes! And this is a good thing. This means that you are helping me find these issues before rolling this out as a full release.

To get into the beta:
Right-click on the game in your library
Choose Properties
Choose Betas
Choose "Super Secret Online Beta" from the dropdown.

This should update your game to the new version. To leave the beta, choose "None" from that same dropdown.

[b]
Please post in the new Hidden in Plain Sight Online Beta forum if you find issues! And if you don't find any issues, please tell me that, too! I'm really anxious about this and want to your success stories.
[/b]

THANK YOU for your help testing this!

notes.title: Hidden in Plain Sight -- Online play for up to 8 players coming soon!
notes.notes:
Hidden in Plain Sight came out nearly 10 years ago for the Xbox Live Indie Gaming platform.

With respect to online gaming, that was a completely different time and place  The Xbox only allowed four players maximum.  We didn't have Discord or other voice/video chat software easily available.  For that and other reasons, HIPS was made as a local multiplayer game.  And it has thrived beyond what I ever expected, thanks to you!

Over the years, the two biggest requests/complaints have been "support more than four players" and "we want to play it online!"  In order to make that happen, I would need to do a full top-to-bottom rewrite of the game.

And, well, I've just done a full top-to-bottom rewrite of the game.  

The game is the essentially the same.  Same game modes.  Same crummy graphics.  A few little tweaks here and there, but the same basic game.

The difference is that the Windows version of Hidden in Plain Sight will soon support 2-8 players and online play.  That could be all local players, one player per computer, or small groups of local players joining other groups of local players.

I swore up and down for years that HIPS would always be a local multiplayer game.  The fact is, with online voice and video chat so accessible these days, you really can get a very good, intimate experience playing online with friends.  It's not quite the same.  Nothing will replace being in the same room with friends.  But for times when that isn't possible, this works.

There is a closed beta going on at the moment while I get rid of some final bugs.  Then I plan to do an open beta for final testing.  And if everything looks good, this version will replace the current version.  

[b]Note that this will just be a free, full in-place update to the existing game.[/b]

This only applies to Windows for now (hopefully with Mac and Linux to follow).  Switch, Xbox One, and other platforms will remain local multiplayer for the foreseeable future.

Comments/questions/concerns?  Let me know what you think.

notes.title: Steam will soon let you play local multiplayer games online
notes.notes:
Oh, the possibilities. Late night TowerFall tournaments, no longer restricted to the too-rare occasions when I’m in the same room as my internet friends. I might get to finish Overcooked 2, this time with a pal who finds efficient cooking more entertaining than winding me up by pretending to mistake fire extinguishers for lettuces. Multiple developers have revealed Valve’s plans for “Remote Play Together”, which will bring automatic online support for local multiplayer games. It’s one more step towards freeing us from the tyranny of geography, with an open beta due for October 21st.

Yeah, you could already do this using third-party tools. But sometimes convenience opens up possibilities by itself.

notes.title: Have you played Hidden In Plain Sight?
notes.notes:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

People are screaming at either side of me. “HE’S THAT ONE AT THE FRONT! SHOOT HIM!” They’re talking about me. I’m staying perfectly still, as though my friend’s vision is based on movement, like a T-Rex. The shot rings out, and all the screaming stops. The last bullet has been fired – not into me, but into an innocent NPC who happened to be looking suspicious at the front of the pack. I’m now free to abandon my statue act and sprint towards the finish line. A great big grin crosses my face at the knowledge that nothing can stop me now.

notes.title: Ninja Party has been updated!
notes.notes:
I never like the "Touch all the Five Statues" win condition on Ninja Party.  The game always ended suddenly with a lot of question marks.

I have modified the rules of Ninja Party.

The original Ninja Party has been renamed "Ninja Party Classic".

Let me know what you think!

notes.title: New game mode -- Ninja Battle Royale
notes.notes:
I added a new game mode to Hidden in Plain Sight.  It's called "Ninja Battle Royale."

It's basically Ninja Party, minus the statutes, and adding a shrinking circle.

Give it a shot and let me know how it goes.  It might be totally dumb, but at least it was free, right?  I think it has the potential for a few laughs.
